$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the public surface of hazardnet.live.
Consumed by two consumers, which is the whole point:
1. scripts/prerender.mjs — emits real HTML (+ <head> metadata) for every route at build time,
so deep links work and crawlers see content without executing JavaScript.
2. the React app (src/components/ArticlePage.tsx + src/hooks/usePageSeo.ts), which renders the
same copy and re-applies the same <head> during client-side navigation.
Editing copy here updates both. Do not fork the text into a component.
Facts in this file are drawn from the repository (README.md, docs/adr/0005-0008,
Models/VERSION.json, scripts/auto_forecast.py). If a claim becomes untrue, fix it here.

site.name: HazardNet
site.defaultTitle: HazardNet — Multi-Hazard Early Warning for Bangladesh Agriculture
site.defaultDescription: HazardNet turns satellite, reanalysis and weather-forecast data into 7- and 15-day multi-hazard outlooks for Bangladesh's 64 districts — 8 hazards, dual-track severity, and free, offline-capable maps.

routes.label: Overview
routes.title: HazardNet — multi-hazard early warning for Bangladesh agriculture
routes.description: Dated, sourced 7- and 15-day hazard outlooks for Bangladesh’s 64 districts: the artifact behind every number, an open hindcast scorecard, and the limits stated. Independent decision support — not an official warning service.
routes.h1: A forecast you can check, not just read
routes.standfirst: HazardNet is an independent, open research platform that turns satellite observations and weather forecasts into 7- and 15-day outlooks for eight climate hazards across Bangladesh’s 64 districts. Every figure it shows comes from a named artifact with a build date, the validation scorecard is published whether it flatters the model or not, and the boundary between this platform and the agencies that issue official warnings is stated on every page.

paragraphs: The operational question in Bangladesh agriculture is rarely whether a hazard is coming; it is which districts, at which crop stage, with how many days of lead time, and how much weight the number deserves. HazardNet is built to answer that second set of questions. For each district and horizon it publishes a hazard class, a severity index, a confidence bin and an independent physics estimate — and the run they came from.
bullets: 64 districts on the live map; the published advisory archive covers 507 ADM3 units (495 upazilas plus 12 city corporations).
Eight hazard classes: cold wave, drought, fire, flash flood, flood, heat wave, severe local storm and tropical cyclone.
Free and non-commercial, with no account needed for the map. The app installs as a PWA, caches its tiles and keeps working when the connection does not.

sections.h2: The current outlook, and where to see it
paragraphs: This page is the record; the live map is the outlook. The split is deliberate and documented, because the two questions need different pages: "where is the hazard now" is answered by a map, and "who produced this, from what, and how would I know if it stopped working" is answered by a document with dates on it.

The strip under the headline reads the committed alert artifact on every load: how many alerts are published at each level, how many districts the last run covered, and how many assessed rows the publication gate withheld. When nothing is published it says so, and says why — silence on a hazard platform is read as safety, so this page does not leave that to be inferred.
bullets: The live map addresses all 64 districts. A district the current run does not cover keeps its static baseline colour and says so on its own page, rather than borrowing a neighbour's number.

Every published alert carries its own evidence: the drivers behind the level, the policy version applied, and whether a duty officer reviewed it or the engine published it on its own at or below its automatic-publishing ceiling.
The status page carries the age of every artifact this deployment ships, measured against the SLO it is held to, together with the notes each run reports against itself.

paragraphs: The pipeline is deliberately narrow so that every step can be inspected. Nothing on this site is written by a language model, and no number is interpolated to fill a gap in a run.
bullets: Inputs: Sentinel-1 radar and Sentinel-2 optical imagery through Google Earth Engine, ERA5-Land reanalysis, Open-Meteo deterministic forecasts, HDX COD-AB administrative boundaries and OpenStreetMap exposure data.
Assembly: one 15-channel tensor per district per forecast date, in a fixed band order, z-scored against the training period.
Inference: a single TFLite pass per unit emits the hazard class, the severity index and the confidence bin. There is one inference path, so two parts of the site cannot disagree.

Cross-check: an independent formula — a vegetation-health index for drought, an excess-heat factor for heat waves, and so on — is computed beside the model and published even when the two tracks diverge.

Publication: the alert engine applies a documented policy and may publish on its own only at or below its configured ceiling — WATCH in this deployment. Anything above that level requires a named duty officer, whose identity is stored on the alert. A run that stamps no model version cannot publish above the ceiling at all, and the engine records publication_blocked rather than issuing the alert.

sections.h2: How to check any number on this site
paragraphs: A claim that cannot be checked is marketing. The platform therefore publishes the evidence next to the claim, including the places where the evidence is thin.
bullets: The status page reads the committed artifacts and states the age of each against its SLO — including when a source is stale, failing or unprovenanced, which is the case the page exists to show.

The validation scorecard reports per-episode detection counts, POD, FAR and CSI for five historical episodes, and states what those metrics cannot support: five episodes are not a validation set, and detection in a hindcast is a ceiling on what the pipeline can see, not a forecast skill score.

The model card lists the known failure modes and the out-of-scope uses, and carries the 2,931-event training claim as reported rather than verified — that archive is not redistributed by this repository, and the pages that would need it say it is absent instead of quoting the figure as if it had been read.
The code, the artifacts and the build scripts are in one public repository, and this site is rebuilt from them: the same pipeline that publishes a number also publishes the check on it.

paragraphs: The dated products this deployment publishes. The reviewed date is the review date the page itself carries, so a stale product can be seen to be stale.

sections.h2: The official record, and where it lives
paragraphs: HazardNet does not issue warnings, cyclone signals or evacuation instructions, and it must never be read as doing so. The bodies that do are named below; their bulletins outrank anything on this site.
bullets: Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) — weather forecasts, cyclone signals, and heat, cold and storm warnings.
Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (FFWC) — river-level forecasts and flood bulletins.
Department of Disaster Management (DDM), Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief — the Standing Orders on Disaster, relief and response.
In an emergency, call the national hotline 999, and follow your local administration’s instructions over anything published here.

links.label: Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief

paragraphs: The platform is maintained as a Master’s thesis project at Bangladesh Agricultural University, and it improves fastest where practitioners push back on it.
bullets: Use it in the field and report where it was wrong. A district, a date and what you observed is enough to act on.
Reuse the data: the download centre carries the forecast snapshot and the offline builds, and the code is MIT-licensed with the citation given on this page.
Report a broken page, a stale run or a prediction that looks wrong from the contact page — every report is read.

faqs.question: Is HazardNet an official warning service?
faqs.answer: No. It is independent decision support for agriculture. Official warnings come from the Bangladesh Meteorological Department for weather hazards, the Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre for river floods, and the Department of Disaster Management with your local administration for response. For an emergency, call 999. HazardNet is meant to give you more lead time to prepare, not to replace those authorities.

faqs.question: How should I cite HazardNet?
faqs.answer: The author, supervisors and institution are given in the attribution block on this page, and the repository ships a CITATION.cff with the same facts in machine-readable form. The code is MIT-licensed; the third-party data behind it keeps its own terms, which the data sources page lists one dataset at a time.

faqs.question: Why is the training archive not published here?
faqs.answer: The model card reports a 2,931-event archive (2000–2025) assembled from third-party records whose own licences govern redistribution. Rather than ship a stale copy that pages would quote as current, the repository ships the loader and the district and season pages state that no archive is loaded. The claim stays a claim until a deployment loads the export.

faqs.question: Is this page available in Bengali?
faqs.answer: Yes — the switch at the top of this page renders the front door's editorial copy and its controls in Bengali. Where a sentence has no Bengali version, the English one is shown rather than a gap: the English copy is the structural authority, so a translation can reword a page but cannot shorten or reorder one. The alert cards, the map and the district tables were translated first; the long-form knowledge products — the model card, the methodology and the data-source ledger — remain English-only.

bn.label: সারসংক্ষেপ
bn.h1: এমন এক পূর্বাভাস, যা আপনি কেবল পড়বেন না — যাচাইও করতে পারবেন
bn.standfirst: HazardNet একটি স্বাধীন ও উন্মুক্ত গবেষণা প্ল্যাটফর্ম, যা উপগ্রহ পর্যবেক্ষণ ও আবহাওয়া পূর্বাভাস থেকে বাংলাদেশের ৬৪টি জেলার জন্য আটটি জলবায়ু-দুর্যোগের ৭ ও ১৫ দিনের পূর্বাভাস তৈরি করে। এতে দেখানো প্রতিটি সংখ্যা একটি নির্দিষ্ট আর্টিফ্যাক্ট থেকে আসে যার নির্মাণ-তারিখ আছে; যাচাই স্কোরকার্ড প্রকাশ করা হয় তা মডেলের পক্ষে যাক বা না যাক; এবং সরকারি সতর্কবার্তা প্রকাশকারী সংস্থাগুলোর সঙ্গে এই প্ল্যাটফর্মের সীমারেখা প্রতিটি পাতায় লেখা থাকে।

paragraphs: বাংলাদেশের কৃষিতে বাস্তব প্রশ্ন খুব কমই এই নয় যে দুর্যোগ আসবে কি না; বরং প্রশ্ন হলো কোন জেলাগুলোতে, ফসলের কোন পর্যায়ে, কত দিনের অগ্রিম বার্তা নিয়ে, এবং সংখ্যাটিকে কতটা গুরুত্ব দেওয়া উচিত। HazardNet তৈরি হয়েছে এই দ্বিতীয় প্রশ্নগুলোর উত্তর দেওয়ার জন্য। প্রতিটি জেলা ও প্রতিটি সময়কালের জন্য এটি প্রকাশ করে একটি দুর্যোগ-শ্রেণি, একটি গুরুতরতা সূচক, একটি আস্থার শ্রেণি ও একটি স্বতন্ত্র ভৌত-নিয়ম অনুমান — সঙ্গে এগুলো কোন রান থেকে এসেছে তার তথ্য।
bullets: লাইভ মানচিত্রে ৬৪টি জেলা; প্রকাশিত পরামর্শ আর্কাইভ আওতা করে ৫০৭টি ADM3 ইউনিট (৪৯৫টি উপজেলা ও ১২টি সিটি কর্পোরেশন)।
আটটি দুর্যোগ-শ্রেণি: শৈতপ্রবাহ, খরা, অগ্নিকাণ্ড, আকস্মিক বন্যা, বন্যা, তাপপ্রবাহ, তীব্র স্থানীয় ঝড় ও ক্রান্তীয় ঘূর্ণিঝড়।
বিনামূল্যে ও অবাণিজ্যিক; মানচিত্র দেখতে কোনো অ্যাকাউন্ট লাগে না। অ্যাপটি PWA হিসেবে ইনস্টল করা যায়, ম্যাপ-টাইল সংরক্ষণ করে এবং সংযোগ না থাকলেও কাজ চালিয়ে যায়।

sections.h2: বর্তমান পূর্বাভাস, এবং তা কোথায় দেখবেন
paragraphs: এই পাতাটি দলিল; লাইভ মানচিত্র হলো পূর্বাভাস। এই বিভাজন ইচ্ছাকৃত ও নথিভুক্ত, কারণ দুটি প্রশ্নের জন্য দুই ধরনের পাতা দরকার: 'দুর্যোগ এখন কোথায়' — এর উত্তর দেয় মানচিত্র; আর 'এটি কে তৈরি করেছে, কী থেকে তৈরি করেছে, এবং কাজ করা বন্ধ করলে আমি তা জানব কীভাবে' — এর উত্তর দেয় তারিখ-সহ একটি দলিল।

শিরোনামের নিচের স্ট্রিপটি প্রতিবার লোড করলে সংরক্ষিত সতর্কবার্তা-আর্টিফ্যাক্ট পড়ে: প্রতিটি স্তরে কতটি সতর্কবার্তা প্রকাশিত, শেষ রান কতটি জেলা আওতা করেছে, এবং প্রকাশনা-গেট মূল্যায়িত কতটি সারি আটকে রেখেছে। কিছু প্রকাশিত না হলে সেটি স্পষ্ট করে বলা হয় এবং কারণও বলা হয় — দুর্যোগ প্ল্যাটফর্মে নীরবতাকে নিরাপত্তা বলে ধরে নেওয়া হয়, তাই এই পাতা সেটি অনুমানের ওপর ছেড়ে দেয় না।
bullets: লাইভ মানচিত্র ৬৪টি জেলার সবগুলোকেই আওতা করে। বর্তমান রানে যেসব জেলার তথ্য নেই, সেগুলো স্থির ভিত্তিমান রঙেই থাকে এবং নিজের পাতায় তা জানিয়ে দেয় — পাশের জেলার সংখ্যা ধার নেয় না।

প্রকাশিত প্রতিটি সতর্কবার্তার সঙ্গে তার নিজস্ব প্রমাণ থাকে: স্তরের পেছনের চালকগুলো, প্রয়োগ হওয়া নীতির সংস্করণ, এবং এটি কোনো দায়িত্বরত কর্মকর্তা পর্যালোচনা করেছেন নাকি ইঞ্জিন স্বয়ংক্রিয়-প্রকাশের সীমার মধ্যে থেকে নিজে প্রকাশ করেছে।
স্ট্যাটাস পাতায় এই ডিপ্লয়মেন্টের প্রতিটি আর্টিফ্যাক্টের বয়স থাকে — যে SLO মেনে চলার কথা তার বিপরীতে মাপা — এবং প্রতিটি রান নিজের বিরুদ্ধে যেসব নোট জানায় তাও থাকে।

paragraphs: পাইপলাইনটি ইচ্ছাকৃতভাবেই সীমিত পরিসরে রাখা হয়েছে যাতে প্রতিটি ধাপ পরীক্ষা করা যায়। এই সাইটের কোনো লেখাই ভাষা-মডেলের লেখা নয়, এবং কোনো সংখ্যাই রানের ফাঁক ভরাট করতে অনুমানে বসানো হয় না।
bullets: ইনপুট: Google Earth Engine-এর মাধ্যমে Sentinel-1 রাডার ও Sentinel-2 অপটিক্যাল চিত্র, ERA5-Land রি-অ্যানালাইসিস, Open-Meteo নির্ধারিত পূর্বাভাস, HDX COD-AB প্রশাসনিক সীমানা ও OpenStreetMap এক্সপোজার তথ্য।
গঠন: প্রতিটি জেলার জন্য প্রতিটি পূর্বাভাস-তারিখে একটি ১৫-চ্যানেল টেনসর, নির্দিষ্ট ব্যান্ড-ক্রমে, প্রশিক্ষণ-কালের সাপেক্ষে z-score করা।
অনুমান: প্রতিটি ইউনিটের জন্য একটি মাত্র TFLite পাস দুর্যোগ-শ্রেণি, গুরুতরতা সূচক ও আস্থার শ্রেণি নির্গত করে। অনুমানের পথ একটিই, তাই সাইটের দুটি অংশ পরস্পরের সঙ্গে অমিল করতে পারে না।
ক্রস-চেক: মডেলের পাশাপাশি একটি স্বতন্ত্র সূত্র — খরার জন্য ভেজিটেশন-হেলথ সূচক, তাপপ্রবাহের জন্য অতিরিক্ত-তাপ ফ্যাক্টর, ইত্যাদি — হিসাব করা হয় এবং দুই ট্র্যাকের ফল মিল না হলেও তা প্রকাশ করা হয়।

প্রকাশনা: সতর্কবার্তা ইঞ্জিন একটি নথিভুক্ত নীতি মেনে চলে এবং নিজ থেকে কেবল নির্ধারিত সীমা পর্যন্ত প্রকাশ করতে পারে — এই ডিপ্লয়মেন্টে সেই সীমা 'সতর্ক দৃষ্টি' (WATCH)। এর ওপরের যেকোনো স্তরের জন্য একজন নাম-উল্লেখিত দায়িত্বরত কর্মকর্তা প্রয়োজন, যাঁর পরিচয় সতর্কবার্তার সঙ্গে সংরক্ষিত থাকে। যে রানে কোনো মডেল-সংস্করণ মুদ্রিত থাকে না, তা এই সীমার ওপরে কিছুই প্রকাশ করতে পারে না; তখন ইঞ্জিন সতর্কবার্তা জারি না করে publication_blocked নথিভুক্ত করে।

sections.h2: এই সাইটের যেকোনো সংখ্যা কীভাবে যাচাই করবেন
paragraphs: যে দাবি যাচাই করা যায় না, সেটি বিপণন। তাই এই প্ল্যাটফর্ম দাবির পাশেই তার প্রমাণ প্রকাশ করে — প্রমাণ যেসব জায়গায় পাতলা, সেসব জায়গাসহ।
bullets: স্ট্যাটাস পাতা সংরক্ষিত আর্টিফ্যাক্টগুলো পড়ে এবং প্রতিটির বয়স তার SLO-র বিপরীতে জানায় — কোনো উৎস পুরনো, ব্যর্থ বা উৎস-পরিচয়বিহীন হলেও, যে অবস্থাটি দেখানোর জন্যই এই পাতাটির অস্তিত্ব।

যাচাই স্কোরকার্ড পাঁচটি ঐতিহাসিক ঘটনার জন্য ঘটনা-প্রতি শনাক্তকরণ সংখ্যা, POD, FAR ও CSI প্রকাশ করে, এবং এই মেট্রিকগুলো কী সমর্থন করতে পারে না তাও বলে: পাঁচটি ঘটনা কোনো যাচাই-সেট নয়, আর হিন্ডকাস্টে শনাক্তকরণ হলো পাইপলাইন কতটুকু দেখতে পারে তার ঊর্ধ্বসীমা — কোনো পূর্বাভাস-দক্ষতার স্কোর নয়।

মডেল কার্ডে জানা ব্যর্থতার ধরন ও ব্যবহারের অযোগ্য ক্ষেত্রগুলো তালিকাভুক্ত, এবং ২,৯৩১ ঘটনার প্রশিক্ষণ-দাবিটি যাচাইকৃত হিসেবে নয়, প্রতিবেদিত হিসেবেই রাখা হয়েছে — এই রিপোজিটরি সেই আর্কাইভ পুনর্বিতরণ করে না, এবং যেসব পাতায় তা দরকার সেগুলো সংখ্যাটি উদ্ধৃত না করে তার অনুপস্থিতিই জানিয়ে দেয়।
কোড, আর্টিফ্যাক্ট ও বিল্ড-স্ক্রিপ্ট একই পাবলিক রিপোজিটরিতে আছে, এবং এই সাইট সেখান থেকেই পুনর্নির্মাণ হয়: যে পাইপলাইন একটি সংখ্যা প্রকাশ করে, সেই পাইপলাইনই তার যাচাইও প্রকাশ করে।

paragraphs: এই ডিপ্লয়মেন্ট যে তারিখ-সহ পণ্যগুলো প্রকাশ করে। পর্যালোচনার তারিখ হলো সেই তারিখ যা পাতাটি নিজেই বহন করে, ফলে একটি পুরনো পণ্যকে পুরনো বলেই চেনা যায়।

sections.h2: সরকারি নথি, এবং তা কোথায় আছে
paragraphs: HazardNet কোনো সতর্কবার্তা, ঘূর্ণিঝড় সংকেত বা আশ্রয়ণ-নির্দেশনা জারি করে না, এবং একে কখনোই তাই মনে করা যাবে না। যেসব সংস্থা এগুলো জারি করে তাদের নাম নিচে দেওয়া; তাদের বুলেটিন এই সাইটের যেকোনো কিছুর চেয়ে অগ্রাধিকার পাবে।
bullets: বাংলাদেশ আবহাওয়া অধিদপ্তর (BMD) — আবহাওয়ার পূর্বাভাস, ঘূর্ণিঝড় সংকেত, এবং তাপ, শৈত ও ঝড় সম্পর্কিত সতর্কবার্তা।
প্লাবন পূর্বাভাস ও সতর্কীকরণ কেন্দ্র (FFWC) — নদীর পানির স্তরের পূর্বাভাস ও বন্যা বুলেটিন।
দুর্যোগ ব্যবস্থাপনা অধিদপ্তর (DDM), দুর্যোগ ব্যবস্থাপনা ও ত্রাণ মন্ত্রণালয় — দুর্যোগ বিষয়ক স্থায়ী আদেশ (Standing Orders on Disaster), ত্রাণ ও সাড়াদান।
জরুরি অবস্থায় জাতীয় হটলাইন ৯৯৯ নম্বরে কল করুন, এবং এখানে প্রকাশিত যেকোনো কিছুর চেয়ে আপনার স্থানীয় প্রশাসনের নির্দেশনা মেনে চলুন।

paragraphs: এই প্ল্যাটফর্মটি বাংলাদেশ কৃষি বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের এক এমএস থিসিস প্রকল্প হিসেবে রক্ষণাবেক্ষণ করা হয়, এবং অনুশীলনকারীরা এর সমালোচনা করলেই এটি সবচেয়ে দ্রুত উন্নত হয়।
bullets: মাঠে ব্যবহার করুন এবং কোথায় ভুল ছিল তা জানান। একটি জেলা, একটি তারিখ আর আপনি কী প্রত্যক্ষ করেছেন — কাজ করার জন্য এটুকুই যথেষ্ট।
তথ্য পুনর্ব্যবহার করুন: ডাউনলোড সেন্টারে পূর্বাভাস স্ন্যাপশট ও অফলাইন বিল্ড আছে, এবং কোড MIT লাইসেন্সযুক্ত — এই পাতায় উদ্ধৃতি দেওয়া আছে।
কোনো পাতা ভাঙা, রান পুরনো বা পূর্বাভাস ভুল মনে হলে যোগাযোগ পাতা থেকে জানান — প্রতিটি রিপোর্ট পড়া হয়।

faqs.question: HazardNet কি কোনো সরকারি সতর্কবার্তা সেবা?
faqs.answer: না। এটি কৃষির জন্য স্বাধীন সিদ্ধান্ত সহায়তা। সরকারি সতর্কবার্তা আসে আবহাওয়া-জনিত দুর্যোগের ক্ষেত্রে বাংলাদেশ আবহাওয়া অধিদপ্তর থেকে, নদীর বন্যার ক্ষেত্রে প্লাবন পূর্বাভাস ও সতর্কীকরণ কেন্দ্র (FFWC) থেকে, এবং সাড়াদানের ক্ষেত্রে দুর্যোগ ব্যবস্থাপনা অধিদপ্তর ও আপনার স্থানীয় প্রশাসন থেকে। জরুরি অবস্থায় ৯৯৯ নম্বরে কল করুন। HazardNet-এর উদ্দেশ্য প্রস্তুতির জন্য আপনাকে বেশি অগ্রিম সময় দেওয়া, ওই কর্তৃপক্ষগুলোর বিকল্প হওয়া নয়।

faqs.question: HazardNet কীভাবে উদ্ধৃত করব?
faqs.answer: লেখক, তত্ত্বাবধায়ক ও প্রতিষ্ঠানের নাম এই পাতার স্বীকৃতি-অংশে দেওয়া আছে, এবং একই তথ্য মেশিন-পাঠযোগ্য রূপে CITATION.cff ফাইলে রিপোজিটরিতে আছে। কোড MIT লাইসেন্সযুক্ত; এর পেছনের তৃতীয় পক্ষের তথ্যের নিজস্ব শর্ত বহাল থাকে, যা তথ্যসূত্র পাতায় একেকটি ডেটাসেট হিসেবে তালিকাভুক্ত।

faqs.question: প্রশিক্ষণ আর্কাইভ কেন এখানে প্রকাশ করা হয়নি?
faqs.answer: মডেল কার্ডে ২,৯৩১ ঘটনার একটি আর্কাইভের (২০০০–২০২৫) কথা বলা হয়েছে, যা তৃতীয় পক্ষের রেকর্ড থেকে সংকলিত এবং যার নিজস্ব লাইসেন্স পুনর্বিতরণ নিয়ন্ত্রণ করে। একটি পুরনো কপি রেখে দেওয়ার চেয়ে — যা পাতাগুলো হালনাগাদ হিসেবে উদ্ধৃত করত — এই রিপোজিটরি লোডারটি সরবরাহ করে, এবং জেলা ও মৌসুমের পাতাগুলো জানিয়ে দেয় যে কোনো আর্কাইভ লোড করা নেই। যতদিন না কোনো ডিপ্লয়মেন্ট এক্সপোর্টটি লোড করে, ততদিন দাবিটি দাবিই থাকে।

faqs.question: এই পাতা কি বাংলায় পাওয়া যায়?
faqs.answer: হ্যাঁ — এই পাতার ওপরের সুইচ ব্যবহার করলে সম্মুখপৃষ্ঠার সম্পাদকীয় লেখা ও নিয়ন্ত্রণগুলো বাংলায় দেখা যাবে। কোনো বাক্যের বাংলা সংস্করণ না থাকলে ফাঁকা না রেখে ইংরেজিটিই দেখানো হয়: ইংরেজি লেখাটিই কাঠামোগত ভিত্তি, তাই অনুবাদ একটি পাতাকে নতুন করে লিখতে পারে কিন্তু সংক্ষিপ্ত বা এলোমেলো করতে পারে না। সতর্কবার্তা কার্ড, মানচিত্র ও জেলার তালিকা আগেই অনূদিত হয়েছে; বিস্তারিত জ্ঞান-পণ্য — মডেল কার্ড, পদ্ধতি ও তথ্যসূত্র খতিয়ান — এখনো ইংরেজিতেই আছে।

routes.label: Live map
routes.title: Live hazard map — 7- and 15-day outlooks for Bangladesh’s 64 districts
routes.description: The HazardNet GIS console: district-level hazard class, severity index, confidence bin and physics cross-check on an offline-capable map, with the run date printed beside it.
routes.standfirst: HazardNet is a free, non-commercial early-warning platform for Bangladesh agriculture. It converts satellite observations, reanalysis data and weather forecasts into 7- and 15-day outlooks for eight climate hazards, then shows them on a map that keeps working when the connection does not.

paragraphs: The interactive map at the top of this page colours each district by the highest-severity hazard of its current outlook, where the latest model run covers it; districts outside that run keep their static baseline colour, and the district card in the dashboard states which of the two is shown. Selecting a district opens its forecast card: hazard type, severity index, confidence bin, the crops and land cover at risk, and the lead time in days.

Every number on the map comes from the most recent forecast snapshot the platform holds. The snapshot's prediction date is printed next to the map — if that date is more than a few days old, treat the outlook as stale and read the banner that explains why.

sections.h2: How to read the numbers honestly
bullets: Severity index (0.00–1.00) is the model's continuous damage-potential score. It is not a probability and not a percentage of damage.

Confidence (Certain ≥ 0.85, Probable 0.70–0.85, Uncertain < 0.70) is the model's own certainty in the hazard class it selected. It is not a measure of whether the forecast is correct, and it is not derived from the physics cross-check — the two tracks are computed separately and can disagree, and each district card shows both side by side so the divergence is visible.

Physics severity is an independent, formula-based estimate (for example, a vegetation-health index for drought or an excess-heat factor for heat waves). Model and physics severity diverging is normal and is shown rather than hidden.

Lead time is the forecast horizon — 7 or 15 days. Both are driven by the same deterministic weather window (Open-Meteo serves at most about 16 days), so the 15-day outlook is the more uncertain of the two and is a planning aid, not a storm-specific prediction. A longer 10/20/30-day horizon set is described in ADR 0005 but is not implemented in the pipeline, so it is not published.

callout.text: HazardNet is decision support, not an official warning service. For evacuation, cyclone signals, flood bulletins and emergency instructions, follow the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD), the Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (FFWC) and your local administration.

paragraphs: Sentinel-1 radar and Sentinel-2 optical imagery (ESA Copernicus, accessed through Google Earth Engine), ERA5-Land reanalysis (ECMWF Copernicus), Open-Meteo deterministic forecasts, HDX COD-AB administrative boundaries and OpenStreetMap exposure data. Full provenance, cadence and licences are on the data sources page.

routes.label: Alerts
routes.title: Live hazard alerts for Bangladesh districts — HazardNet
routes.description: Published HazardNet alerts by district: level, hazard, 7- and 15-day horizon, the evidence behind each one, and the policy that decides it. Available in Bengali and English, and it keeps working offline.
routes.standfirst: Every alert HazardNet has published, district by district, with the evidence and the policy behind it. A watch is the highest level the engine can publish on its own; anything above a watch waits for a named duty officer to approve it. The list is rendered from live data, so this page also works from the snapshot the deployment carries when the API cannot be reached.

paragraphs: Four levels are published: no alert, watch, warning and severe. The level comes from the alert policy in force, not from the model alone. A watch is issued when the model score crosses the watch threshold or when its severity band does; a warning additionally requires a calibrated probability, and no calibration map is fitted for the current model version, so warnings are not currently issuable from model evidence.
Each alert states the hazard class, the district, the 7- or 15-day horizon, the forecast issue time, the data cutoff and the model version it came from.

Every alert carries a model severity, an independently computed physics severity and the divergence between the two tracks. When the tracks disagree beyond the policy threshold the alert is flagged rather than silently averaged.

The model score is a softmax output used as a relative priority signal. It is not a probability that the hazard will occur, and no calibration map is fitted yet — the alert page says this next to every number.

The engine publishes at or below the watch level automatically. A warning or severe alert requires a named duty officer, a review timestamp and the model version and data cutoff recorded against the decision, so a published alert can always be traced back to the run that produced it.

Alerts are also delivered by SMS and Telegram to subscribers who have opted in. Both channels carry the same disclaimer as this page, and a single SMS is capped at 70 Bengali characters per segment, which is why the message body is short and links back to the evidence card.

routes.label: Methodology
routes.title: Methodology — how HazardNet builds a forecast
routes.description: The full HazardNet pipeline: satellite and reanalysis inputs, the 15-channel tensor, TFLite inference, dual-track severity, confidence binning, horizons, freshness policy and what is — and is not — validated.
routes.standfirst: Everything HazardNet does between a satellite pass and the district card on your screen, including the parts that are uncertain, delayed or not yet validated. If you are going to make a decision with this platform, this page is the one to read.

paragraphs: The pipeline runs from a scheduled GitHub Actions workflow on HazardNet's own runners — no third-party notebook service is in the critical path. For each forecast unit it assembles a 15-channel spatio-temporal tensor from four families of input:
bullets: Radar — Sentinel-1 GRD backscatter (VV and VH), which sees the surface through cloud and is the primary flood signal.
Optical — Sentinel-2 surface reflectance, reduced to vegetation and water indices (NDVI, NDWI). Cloud cover is the limiting factor and is treated as missing data, not as zero.
Reanalysis — ERA5-Land fields: 2 m temperature (mean, max, min), dewpoint, soil water content at multiple depths, solar radiation, wind speed.
Forecast — Open-Meteo deterministic daily weather for the lead-time window (see the horizon caveat in section 4).

paragraphs: The tensor feeds a 3D depthwise-separable convolutional network that emits two heads: an 8-class softmax over the hazard taxonomy (cold wave, drought, fire, flash flood, flood, heat wave, severe local storm, tropical cyclone) and a continuous severity regression. The same FP32 TFLite bundle that runs on the server runs in a visitor's browser through TensorFlow.js WASM, which is what makes the offline and low-bandwidth experience possible.

A single neural network returning a confident-looking number is not enough for an early-warning product, so every output carries a second, formula-based estimate beside it: a rainfall threshold for flood and flash flood, a vegetation-health index for drought, an excess-heat factor for heat wave. The two tracks are published side by side rather than blended. Two limits are stated plainly, and each published record carries the evidence of which one applied to it. In forecasts published before 17 September 2026 the physics track was computed only for the hazard class the model selected, so it could check the model's magnitude but not its choice of hazard, and it could not independently detect a hazard the model had missed; those records are still shown and are stamped with the pipeline version that produced them. From that date the pipeline scores all eight hazard classes from the weather drivers alone and publishes what the physics track picks on its own (physics_top_hazard and the per-class physics_scores), so a hazard the model misses is visible in the data rather than only inferable from a severity gap.

The confidence bin on each record is the model's own certainty in the class it selected; it is not derived from track agreement, so a high confidence is possible while the two tracks disagree. Where they diverge, both values stay visible on the district card. A high model severity against a low physics severity means 'the model sees something the physics estimate does not' — treat it as a question to verify, not as an alarm. Deriving confidence from the two tracks instead of the softmax is a planned change, not a shipped behaviour.

Outlooks are published at 7 and 15 days, both driven by the same deterministic weather-forecast window; Open-Meteo serves at most about 16 deterministic days, so the 15-day outlook inherits that window's uncertainty. They are planning aids for seasonal decisions such as irrigation, planting and stock movement, not storm-specific predictions. A 10/20/30-day horizon set is specified in ADR 0005 but has not been implemented in the pipeline, and the website does not advertise it.

A refresh is attempted hourly; the published result is a committed snapshot that the website can serve even when the API or the pipeline is unavailable (ADR 0008). The platform therefore degrades to 'older data' rather than to 'no data' — and it labels the age of what it is showing. If the pipeline stalls, the snapshot keeps serving until a newer one replaces it, and the site-health probe raises the alarm in CI.

callout.text: Read the prediction date, not the page-load time. A page that loaded one second ago can still be showing an outlook computed days ago.

sections.h2: 6 · What is validated — and what is not
bullets: Validated in CI: the TFLite bundle loads, labels and normalisation statistics are present, and the bundle is not served publicly.
Checked at runtime: freshness of the served snapshot, with a hard failure in the health probe when the data is older than the freshness threshold.
Cross-checked: model severity versus physics severity for every unit and horizon.

Not yet validated: forecast skill against observed hazard outcomes. HazardNet does not currently publish a hit rate, false-alarm rate or Brier score against BMD/FFWC records. Until it does, treat severity as a relative prioritisation signal rather than a calibrated probability.

paragraphs: The pipeline scripts, model bundle manifest, database migrations and ADRs are in the public repository. Forecast archives are published as release artifacts, and the history API exposes past prediction dates for comparison.

routes.label: Model card
routes.title: Model card — HazardNet multi-hazard classifier
routes.description: Architecture, inputs, outputs, precision, intended use, out-of-scope uses, known failure modes and reporting channels for the HazardNet multi-hazard classification model (FP32 TFLite).
routes.standfirst: A model card for the classifier that produces HazardNet's hazard labels and severity indices: what it is, what it must not be used for, and where it is known to fail.

bullets: Task: multi-label climate-hazard classification plus continuous severity regression per forecast unit, per horizon.
Hazard classes (8): cold wave, drought, fire, flash flood, flood, heat wave, severe local storm, tropical cyclone.
Input: 15-channel spatio-temporal tensor (Sentinel-1 VV/VH, Sentinel-2 indices, ERA5-Land surface and soil state, precipitation and wind from Open-Meteo).
Architecture: 3D depthwise-separable convolutional network with a shared trunk and two heads — 8-way softmax classification and severity regression.
Bundle: FP32 TFLite, roughly 0.75 MB and refreshed by the pipeline.
Execution: server-side for scheduled runs, and in the visitor's browser through TensorFlow.js WASM for interactive and offline use.

paragraphs: HazardNet is built for agricultural extension officers, NGOs and disaster-management practitioners in Bangladesh who need a consistent national picture at district and sub-district level, and for researchers who need a transparent, citation-friendly baseline. It is a prioritisation and situational-awareness tool: it helps you decide where to look next and which district to call.

sections.h2: Out of scope — do not use it for this
bullets: Issuing or replacing official warnings. Cyclone signals, flood bulletins and evacuation orders come from BMD, FFWC and the local administration.
Any decision where a false negative costs lives without a human check — the model is a screening layer, not an authority.
Property, insurance or compensation determinations; the severity index is not a damage assessment.
Sub-district micro-siting. The outlook is published per administrative unit; it does not resolve individual fields, roads or embankments.
Cloud and scan gaps: Sentinel-2 optical input is missing under persistent cloud, and Sentinel-1 revisit is not instantaneous, so a fast-onset event between passes can be under-observed.
Reanalysis lag: ERA5-Land is a reanalysis product with its own latency; the most recent hours are estimated, not measured.
Proxy physics: the independent severity track uses formula proxies. A proxy can be wrong in the same direction as the model, which weakens the cross-check as an error detector.
Class imbalance: rare hazards (for example, severe local storms) have fewer training examples than floods, so their calibration is weaker.
Long horizons: the 15-day outlook inherits the uncertainty of a deterministic weather window and should be read as an outlook, not a prediction.
No INT8 edge bundle exists: a 3D-convolution quantisation path is closed by the runtime at FP32-only precision (ADR 0007). Older documents that mention an INT8 sub-2 MB bundle are out of date.

paragraphs: The model consumes environmental data only — no personal data, no farm-level records and no household information enter training or inference. Account data used by the dashboard (profile, saved districts, connectors) is separate from the model and is not used as model input.

sections.h2: Reporting a problem with a prediction
paragraphs: If a district card looks wrong — a missed event, an over-stated severity, a stale date — send it to the team with the district, hazard, horizon and date. Ground-truth reports are the only route by which the platform can eventually publish skill metrics.

routes.label: Data sources
routes.title: Data sources, licences and update cadence — HazardNet
routes.description: Every dataset behind HazardNet — Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 via Google Earth Engine, ERA5-Land, Open-Meteo, HDX COD-AB boundaries, OpenStreetMap — with licences, cadence and known latency.
routes.standfirst: HazardNet is only as good as the data underneath it. This page lists every input, who produces it, how often it updates, what it costs the user (nothing) and what its licence requires of anyone republishing it.

bullets: Sentinel-1 GRD, C-band SAR (VV/VH) — ESA Copernicus, accessed through Google Earth Engine. All-weather surface backscatter; the primary flood and surface-water signal. Revisit of roughly 6–12 days at Bangladesh latitudes, depending on the constellation and orbit.

Sentinel-2 MSI, Level-2A surface reflectance — ESA Copernicus, via Google Earth Engine. Vegetation and water indices (NDVI, NDWI) for drought and crop stress. 5-day nominal revisit, cloud-limited during the monsoon.

ERA5-Land hourly reanalysis — ECMWF, via the Copernicus Climate Data Store / Earth Engine. Temperature (mean, max, min), dewpoint, soil water at multiple depths, solar radiation, wind. Complete spatial coverage with a latency of several days for the most recent hours.
Open-Meteo deterministic forecast — Open-Meteo (CC-BY 4.0). Daily temperature, precipitation, wind, dewpoint, radiation and evapotranspiration for the lead-time window, up to about 16 days.
HDX COD-AB administrative boundaries — OCHA / HDX. The 64-district (ADM2) and 507-unit (ADM3: 495 upazilas plus 12 city corporations) geometry that every forecast is attached to (ADR 0005).
OpenStreetMap exposure overlay — OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL). Roads, bridges and other infrastructure intersecting a hazard footprint, used for the exposure view (ADR 0006).

paragraphs: HazardNet links out to the institutions that carry legal responsibility for warnings in Bangladesh. Their bulletins always take precedence over anything shown here:
bullets: Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) — weather forecasts, cyclone signals, heat and cold alerts.
Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (FFWC) — river-level and flood bulletins.
Department of Disaster Management (DDM) — national disaster directives and shelter information.
National emergency hotline: 999.

sections.h2: Attribution and licence notes for reusers
bullets: Copernicus data (Sentinel-1/2, ERA5-Land) is free to use with attribution to the European Union's Copernicus programme and ESA/ECMWF as appropriate.
Open-Meteo data is CC-BY 4.0: attribute Open-Meteo when republishing derived values.
OpenStreetMap data is ODbL: derived databases must carry the same licence and attribution.
HazardNet's own code is MIT-licensed; the forecast archive is published as release artifacts with a sha256 manifest so a republication can be traced to an exact run.

paragraphs: The value added is the assembly and the cross-checking: a harmonised 15-channel tensor per unit, one inference pass that produces a comparable severity index across all 64 districts, an independent physics-based severity track beside it, and a confidence bin that tells you whether the two agree.

routes.label: FAQ
routes.title: HazardNet FAQ — accuracy, freshness, offline use and official warnings
routes.description: Straight answers about HazardNet: is it an official warning, what the percentage means, how fresh the data is, whether it works offline, how exports are scoped and how to report a wrong forecast.
routes.standfirst: The questions visitors actually ask, answered without marketing language — including the ones about what HazardNet cannot do.

faqs.question: Is HazardNet an official government warning service?
faqs.answer: No. HazardNet is an independent, non-commercial decision-support platform. Cyclone signals, flood bulletins, evacuation orders and emergency instructions are issued by the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD), the Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (FFWC), the Department of Disaster Management (DDM) and your local administration. Always follow them over anything shown here. The national emergency hotline is 999.

faqs.question: What does the percentage next to a district actually mean?
faqs.answer: It is the model's severity index, scaled 0–100 for display. It is a continuous score of damage potential for the forecast unit and horizon — not a probability, and not a forecast that X% of the district will be damaged. The underlying value runs from 0.00 to 1.00 and is shown with the physics-based severity estimate beside it.

faqs.question: What is the difference between severity, confidence and physics severity?
faqs.answer: Severity is the model's damage-potential score. Physics severity is a formula-based estimate (for example a rainfall threshold for flood, an excess-heat factor for heat waves). Records published before 17 September 2026 computed it only for the hazard class the model selected, so it checked the model's magnitude rather than its choice of hazard; from that date all eight hazard classes are scored from the weather drivers alone and the class the physics track would have picked is published beside the model's. Confidence is the model's own certainty in that class: Certain at 0.85 and above, Probable between 0.70 and 0.85, Uncertain below 0.70. It does not measure agreement between the two tracks; when they diverge, both values stay visible on the card and the outlook should be treated as a question to verify rather than an alarm.

faqs.question: How fresh is the data, and how often is it updated?
faqs.answer: A refresh is attempted hourly and the published result is a committed snapshot. The prediction date is printed next to the map, and that date — not the time you opened the page — tells you how old the outlook is. If the pipeline fails, the site keeps serving the last good snapshot and labels its age rather than showing nothing.

faqs.question: Which hazards and which areas are covered?
faqs.answer: Eight hazards: cold wave, drought, fire, flash flood, flood, heat wave, severe local storm and tropical cyclone. The interactive map covers all 64 districts of Bangladesh, and the published archive covers 507 sub-district (ADM3) units — 495 upazilas plus 12 city corporations — using HDX COD-AB boundaries.

faqs.question: How far ahead can it really see?
faqs.answer: HazardNet publishes 7- and 15-day outlooks, both driven by the same deterministic weather forecast window (Open-Meteo serves at most about 16 days). They are honest planning aids for seasonal decisions (irrigation, planting, stock movement), not storm-specific long-range predictions — read the 15-day outlook as the more uncertain of the two.

faqs.question: Does HazardNet work offline?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the limits are worth knowing. The app installs as a PWA and caches map tiles you have already viewed, so previously visited areas can render without a connection. New forecasts, new areas and any export you have not generated before need a connection. Cached tiles are held in browser storage with a size cap, so a long time offline — or clearing site data — will empty the cache.

faqs.question: What exactly does a map or PDF export contain?
faqs.answer: The export captures the current view: the layers you have enabled, the district or region in frame, the prediction date, the legend, data attribution and the disclaimer. Resolution and page size are chosen in the export dialog before the file is generated, and the dialog states what will be in the filename, format and date range.

faqs.question: What happens to my data if I create an account?
faqs.answer: An account stores the profile fields you fill in, your saved districts, your connectors and your preferences so the dashboard can show them to you. Environmental forecasts do not depend on your account, and no personal data is used as model input. See the privacy policy for retention and deletion.

faqs.question: A district card looks wrong. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Send it in: district, hazard, horizon, date and what you observed on the ground. Ground-truth reports are the only route by which the platform can publish skill metrics, and they are how thresholds get corrected. Use the contact page, which reaches the maintainers directly.

routes.label: System status
routes.title: HazardNet system status — data freshness, coverage and the last health probe
routes.description: What this deployment ships right now: the age of the forecast snapshot and the alert snapshot against their SLOs, the coverage of the current run, model provenance (not stamped yet), and the last published site-health probe result. Every number is copied from a named committed file, and anything unknown is labelled unknown.
routes.standfirst: This page is built from the artifacts the deployment ships — the forecast snapshot, the ingest manifest, the alert snapshot and the last site-health probe result — not from a live probe of the running services. It states the age of each source against the SLO it is measured against, the coverage of the current run, the model provenance, and what the last probe run found. Where a value is unknown, it says unknown.

paragraphs: The numbers above are derived from four committed files: the website forecast snapshot, the ingest run manifest, the alert snapshot and, when one has been published, the site-health probe result. A build script turns them into one artifact, served at /data/freshness.json: that is what this page renders, and what a script or a monitoring system can read.
The derived timestamp printed above each table is when that artifact was produced. It moves when the pipeline commits new data, when the probe commits a new result, and when the site is rebuilt.

bullets: Within SLO — the source is present and its age is inside the SLO that applies to it: 192 hours for the forecast data, 48 hours for the alert snapshot, 2 hours for the probe result.
Past SLO — the source is present but older than its SLO. The age and the SLO are both printed so the gap can be read directly.
Checks failing — the last site-health probe run reported at least one failed check; the checks table names them.
No data — the artifact the source describes is not present in this deployment at all. No age is printed, because there is nothing to age.

Unknown — the artifact could not be read, or it does not carry the timestamp the age would need. Unknown is a distinct state from No data on purpose: one means the file is missing, the other means we cannot tell.

sections.h2: What this page deliberately does not claim
bullets: It is not an uptime or availability report. No uptime history is kept and no percentage is computed here; the site-health probe reports an outcome per check, per run, and that is what it says.
It is not a live probe. A source can be Within SLO here while the deployed site is failing its checks — the probe row, not the freshness rows, is the live-surface signal.

It does not name missing districts when the run did not report them. The coverage stamp says how many districts the run covered; if the run did not list which ones are absent, this page says so rather than inferring them.

It does not describe a model version that does not exist. While the ingest pipeline does not stamp a model_version, the provenance row says Not stamped, and the alert engine's publication gate stays closed for everything above WATCH.
It is not an official warning service. Read the methodology page for scope, and heed the warnings issued by BMD, FFWC, DDM and your local administration.

callout.text: Within SLO on this page describes the committed data files the deployment ships, not the services that serve them. For the live surface — the homepage, deep links, security headers, the sitemap and the forecast endpoint — read the last site-health probe result in the table above or the Site Health Probe workflow run it links to.

faqs.question: How often is this page updated?
faqs.answer: Whenever the data it describes is committed: the scheduled forecast pipeline commits a new snapshot (and therefore a new derived artifact) when it runs, the site-health probe commits its result every 30 minutes on the default branch, and every deployment rebuilds the page from whatever artifact is committed at that commit. The derived timestamp printed with the tables is the authoritative answer for the copy you are reading.

faqs.question: Why does the model version say Not stamped?
faqs.answer: Because the ingest pipeline does not currently record a model_version on the rows it publishes, and this page will not print one it cannot prove. The same absence is why nothing above the WATCH level can be published automatically yet: the product spec requires a model version on a published alert, and the engine records that as a blocker instead of issuing one.

faqs.question: The alert list is empty — is that an error?
faqs.answer: No. The alert engine assessed the current run's rows and published none of them, because none of them had the model provenance a published alert requires. The count of assessed rows that produced no published alert is stated in the notes above, so an empty list is visible as a state rather than as a silent absence.

faqs.question: Does Within SLO mean the site is up?
faqs.answer: No. Within SLO is a statement about the age of a data file against its threshold. Whether the deployed site serves its pages, its headers and its API is what the site-health probe checks, and its result is reported separately above.

routes.standfirst: HazardNet is a free multi-hazard early-warning platform for Bangladesh agriculture, built around satellite observation, open data and an explicitly honest treatment of uncertainty.

bullets: 64 districts on the interactive map; 507 ADM3 units in the published archive.
Eight hazards: cold wave, drought, fire, flash flood, flood, heat wave, severe local storm, tropical cyclone.
7- and 15-day horizons with confidence bins, dual-track severity and a physics cross-check.

paragraphs: Core forecasting is free and does not require an account. The blog carries advertising, which is the only monetised surface, and account features are optional. No hazard data is behind a paywall.

routes.standfirst: Four settings where the outlook is read differently, because the hazard, the lead time that matters and the decision being made are all different.

bullets: Haor pre-monsoon flash flood — short lead time, boro harvest timing, road and embankment access.

sections.h2: What to send with a report
bullets: District or upazila, hazard and the forecast horizon you are looking at.
The prediction date shown on the page you saw — freshness matters more than page-load time.
What you observed on the ground, and roughly when.
A contact address if you want a reply; reports are used to correct thresholds and to build published skill metrics.

callout.text: This is not an emergency channel and it is not monitored around the clock. In an emergency call 999, and follow BMD, FFWC, DDM and local administration instructions.

routes.title: Privacy policy — HazardNet
routes.description: What HazardNet stores, why it stores it, how long it is kept and how to have it deleted. Environmental forecasting needs no personal data.
routes.standfirst: HazardNet forecasts run on environmental data, not on your data. This page explains the narrow set of things an account does store.

bullets: No account is required to read any forecast, map or advisory.
An account stores only the profile fields you enter, your saved districts, connector settings and preferences.
Personal data is never used as model input, and is not sold or shared for advertising.
Advertising is limited to the blog and is served by Google AdSense when configured; core hazard content carries no ads.

routes.label: Terms
routes.title: Terms of use — HazardNet
routes.description: The terms for using HazardNet, including the disaster early-warning disclaimer: decision support only, never a substitute for official BMD, FFWC or DDM instructions.
routes.standfirst: Short version: use the platform freely, cite the data, and treat every forecast as decision support rather than an official instruction.

paragraphs: HazardNet predictions, severity indices and advisories are generated by automated models for decision support. They do not supersede or replace official emergency evacuation orders, cyclone warnings or river-level bulletins issued by the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD), the Flood Forecasting and Warning Centre (FFWC), the Department of Disaster Management (DDM) or local authorities. Forecasts carry uncertainty that is stated rather than hidden; verify before acting and never use this platform as the sole basis for a life-safety decision.

routes.label: Hazard archive
routes.title: Historical hazard archive for Bangladesh, 2000–2025
routes.description: 2,931 recorded event-district observations across Bangladesh's 64 districts and eight hazard classes, grouped into 251 physical episodes, with every data-quality limit stated on the page.
routes.standfirst: Every hazard record this platform holds for Bangladesh between 2000 and 2025, grouped so the numbers can be read for what they are. The archive holds 2,931 event-district observations covering 64 districts and eight hazard classes. Those rows describe 251 distinct physical episodes, because a national event is recorded once per district — a row is an observation, not a disaster. The page states the archive's own limits: which year is missing, how far its hazard labels disagree with the GLIDE identifiers, and which columns carried no information at all.

sections.h2: What the archive records, and what a row means
paragraphs: The archive is a compilation of dated hazard events for Bangladesh, assembled from third-party records and loaded through this repository's own event contract. Each row is one district on one date for one hazard class. That unit matters: a cyclone that crossed the coast and affected all 64 districts appears as 64 rows and one physical episode. Reading the row count as a count of disasters overstates the record by roughly an order of magnitude, so the observation count and the episode count are printed next to each other everywhere on this site.

Rows are grouped into episodes by their public GLIDE event identifier where one exists. Of the 251 episodes, 41 are national in coverage and 18 are partial; 192 rows carry no GLIDE identifier at all and are grouped by date and hazard class instead.

sections.h2: What the archive does not record
bullets: The year 2001 is entirely absent from the archive. A gap in a hazard record is a gap in reporting, not a quiet year, and the timeline on the archive page says so rather than plotting zero.
The source archive's casualty field is zero for every row, which means 'not recorded' rather than 'nobody was affected'. No page on this site publishes an affected or death figure from it.

The archive's hazard label and its GLIDE identifier disagree on 846 rows, most often between severe local storm and tropical cyclone, or between flood and flash flood. Both values are preserved and the disagreement is reported rather than reconciled.
Three source columns are constant across all 2,931 rows and carry no information. The loader refuses to map them, so they cannot be mistaken for data.

paragraphs: The figures on the archive page are read from a published artifact built by this repository's build scripts from a validated load of the source archive, not computed in the browser. The loader enforces the same event contract as every other hazard source this platform ingests, and the build refuses to publish an artifact whose counts no longer agree with the data it was built from. The artifact carries aggregate counts, public GLIDE identifiers and summary statistics only: no per-row records, no coordinates and none of the source's descriptive text, because the source compilation is not redistributed here.

A severity index derived from this archive, together with its weighting scheme, is part of unpublished research and is withheld from public copy until the associated publication is released. The archive page states this explicitly rather than leaving an unexplained gap. The severity statistics that are published alongside the archive are computed from the severity values the source archive itself reports, and are labelled as such wherever they appear.
